rows.verified: Passengers should pay attention to the safety briefing because exits and equipment differ between aircraft.
CAA recommends keeping the seat belt fastened throughout the flight.
Seat-belt use is mandatory when the illuminated sign is on, including during turbulence.
Seat belts should be adjusted for a secure but comfortable fit with the buckle accessible.
Sleeping passengers should fasten the seat belt over a blanket so cabin crew can see it is secured.
Passengers should remain seated and belted until the sign is switched off after landing.
In an emergency evacuation passengers must follow crew instructions and leave cabin baggage behind.
Passengers should identify their nearest exit, which may be behind them.
Turbulence injury risk depends on intensity, warning time, passenger movement, restraint use, cabin service, aircraft phase and crew response.
CAA cabin evidence is flight-, aircraft-, passenger-, restraint-, weather- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.
ORR guidance provides a structured approach for rail companies to manage fatigue risk.
Employers must assess and control risks from staff fatigue under general health-and-safety law and rail-specific requirements.
Controllers of safety-critical work must prevent work where fatigue could significantly affect safety.
ORR recommends a proportionate Fatigue Risk Management System covering safety-critical and other work.
All dutyholders require basic fatigue controls even without shift work or significant overtime.
A formal FRMS is particularly relevant to shift work, long hours, dangerous machinery, moving vehicles, work at height and electrical work.
Dutyholders should establish a fatigue policy as part of or alongside the wider health-and-safety policy.
Fatigue can reduce vigilance, attention, reaction time and decision quality, increasing human-error risk.
Rail fatigue risk depends on roster, shift timing, overtime, travel, workload, sleep opportunity, individual factors, reporting and safety culture.
ORR fatigue evidence is worker-, roster-, task-, organisation-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level incident probability.
